closeout.reason: User confirmed closure after implementation, full verification, exact-source review, and inspection.
closeout.summary: Verified one Commerce-owned append-only atomic first-registration claim per catalog product setup generation; simultaneous contenders converge on one hidden operation and winning pool, losing requests cannot overwrite it, and unavailable or ambiguous claim authority fails closed before Commerce persistence or Inventory contact. The exact pool-specific feedback and temporary-unavailability copy are exported. EmDash 0.35 and Wrangler/D1 multi-process proofs passed, as did exact Inventory PR 12 retry compatibility, 56 unit/contract tests, 12 integration tests, TypeScript, public-repository and feature audits. Review was clean at sha256:59ae7b56d8e41c458e380d225fb335ed07edbc95a0d164ccbe0db5010d0aa223. No choices were superseded and none were deferred. Remaining disclosed integration work is later disable/re-enable generation ownership and catalog-route reconciliation if a winner stops after claim commit; live Inventory transport, UI, deployment, and production behavior remain excluded. No delivery action was authorized or performed.

current_focus.summary: Implement a Commerce-owned atomic first-registration claim behind a provider-neutral persistence port. Persist one append-only claim per product/setup generation before Inventory contact, let exactly one contender call Inventory, return every loser to the winning operation with pool-specific pending or complete feedback and a Refresh status action, reject conflicting winner replacement, and fail closed with no provider call when atomic uniqueness cannot be proven. Preserve rejected-operation resubmission with a new operation ID. Prove same-input and conflicting-input races across separate processes on exact EmDash 0.35 storage plus missing-constraint failure; exclude admin UI, live Inventory transport, pool discovery, stock mutation, checkout, delivery, and production changes.

decisions.choice: Commerce must atomically converge every simultaneous first-enable attempt for one catalog product on one persisted hidden registration operation ID. Exactly one operation ID wins; all competing attempts resolve to that same winner and may not create a second logical Inventory registration.

decisions.question: What identity may persist when simultaneous requests first enable managed stock for the same Commerce catalog product?
decisions.rationale: The Commerce catalog product is the ownership boundary. A single durable winning identity prevents duplicate registrations while preserving safe retries under the already-locked Inventory command-id contract.

decisions.choice: When a simultaneous managed-stock request resolves to another request's winning operation, Commerce retains the winner and creates no second logical registration. The feedback must name the winning pool. When complete: 'This product was connected to {poolName} in another session. Refresh to review its inventory settings.' When pending: 'This product is already being connected to {poolName} in another session. Refresh to check its status.' A Refresh status action reloads the authoritative Commerce state. If the losing request proposed different settings, it must not overwrite or silently replace the winning pool configuration.

history.choice: Commerce should join the existing winning operation instead of showing an error, then present state-specific feedback with a Refresh status action. When complete: 'Inventory setup for this SKU was completed in another session. Refresh to see the current stock settings.' When pending: 'Inventory setup for this SKU was started in another session and is still in progress. Refresh to check its status.'

decisions.question: What should an agent see after its simultaneous managed-stock request resolves to another request's winning operation?
decisions.rationale: Naming the actual pool tells the agent what became authoritative. State-specific language avoids falsely claiming completion, and requiring refresh/review protects the one-active-pool-per-store binding when simultaneous requests disagree.

decisions.choice: Fail closed before contacting Inventory. Create and send no new operation ID, do not transition the product beyond its last durable state, and show: 'Inventory setup is temporarily unavailable. Please try again.' A later explicit retry may attempt the atomic claim again; Commerce must not substitute an in-process-only mutex or best-effort save.

decisions.question: What should Commerce do when its active persistence surface cannot guarantee one atomic registration claim for the product?
decisions.rationale: Temporarily blocking setup is safer than allowing separate server copies to create duplicate logical registrations. The restriction applies only to beginning managed-stock setup when atomic authority is unavailable.

alternatives: Begin the private Commerce-to-Inventory service-binding adapter first.
recommendation.reason: The route makes the proven claim callable from a catalog product, owns durable setup-generation selection, and recovers a committed winner into authoritative Commerce state while keeping the live Inventory transport replaceable during EmDash 1.0 changes.
recommendation.recommended: Grill the authenticated Commerce managed-stock setup route and winner reconciliation against the atomic claim port.
